 *******
 Judgment

The petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a road traffic accident filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V. Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of a moped No.KA-52-R-8514 alleging that 19.09.2020 at 10.00 PM when riding the motorcycle No.KA-05-JK-6048 on Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-4 near T.Begur in front of T.C.I. Gowdown, Nagamangala Taluk, rider of the moped No. KA-52-R-8514 drove the same from opposite direction negligently dashed the same to motorcycle No. KA-05-JK-6048 thereby caused accident caused injuries to the petitioner.

Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital,
Nelamangala, KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru by spending Rs.1,95,000/-.
As on the date of the accident petitioner being aged 23 years use to earn Rs.17,000/- per month by working in a private company.

Regarding the accident Nelamangala Traffic Police registered Crime No.334/2020 against the rider of the moped for having committed the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
2.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground that the person who drove the moped during accident had no license to drive the moped.
3. Inspite of the service of the notice, respondent No.1 owner of the moped remained absent.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 14.06.2022 this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing No.KA-52-R-8514 by its rider dashed to the petitioner who was riding the Bajaj Discovery motor cycle bearing reg. No. KA-05-JK-6048 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.09.2020?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of petitioner himself?

3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order?

On 04.07.2023 petitioner produced evidence of Dr. Ravish V.N. as PW.2 Manu.B vs Manjula on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98781910/
2 and get produced 4 documents at Exs.P.158 to P.161.

On 26.07.2023, 12.08.2023,
respondent No.2 insurance company produced evidence of the Officer as RW.1 and produced four documents at Ex.R1 to R4.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.
7. Learned advocate appearing for petitioner filed notes of arguments along with four judgments.
8. Learned advocate appearing for respondent No.2 filed copy of three judgments.

9. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
In the Negative, Issue No.3...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.4,73,700/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from respondent No.1 Issue No.4 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 & 2:-

In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that on 19.09.2020 at 10.00 PM when riding the motorcycle No.KA-05-JK-6048 from Tumkur-Bengaluru near T.Begur in front of TCI Godown, Nagamangala, rider of the moped No.KA-52-R-8514 drove the same from opposite direction negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle No. KA-05-JK-6048 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to petitioner and caused damage to the motorcycle.

Petitioner further stated that his brother-in-law who rode the motorcycle No. KA-05-JK- 6048 behind him, witnessed the accident noted the registration number of the moped which caused the accident, shifted to Government Hospital, Nelamangala wherein first aid was provided then shifted to KIMS, Bengaluru.
11.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of accident.

12. In the cross-examination, petitioner/PW.1 stated that the motorcycle rode by him during the accident was owned by Shivaprakash friend of his uncle and during accident he was riding the motor cycle at 30 to 40 Kms per hour.
PW.1 stated that he saw the motorcycle No. KA-52-R- 8514 at a distance of about 30 to 40 feet prior to the accident.
PW.1 stated that Manjunath son of his uncle filed the complaint and Manjunath was riding another motorcycle behind his motorcycle.
PW.1 admitted that in the complaint it is noted that the accident taken place due to head on collusion between motorcycle rode by him and another motorcycle No. KA-52-R-8514.
PW.1 submitted Manu.B vs Manjula on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98781910/
3 ignorance about the person against whom the police have filed the charge sheet.
13. In the evidence PW.2 Dr. Ravish V.N. stated nothing regarding the reason and mode of the accident.
14. In the evidence RW.1 Officer of the Insurance Company stated about non-possessing of license to ride the motorcycle or moped by the person against whom police have filed the charge sheet.

15. Ex.P1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint registered by Nelamangala Traffic Police pertaining to Crime No.334/2020 on 20.09.2020 against the rider of the moped No. KA-52-R-8514 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279 & 337 of IPC, regarding the accident taken place on 19.09.2020 at 10 PM between motorcycle No. KA-05-JK-6048 and moped No.KA-52-R- 8514 resulting in the injuries to the petitioner on the basis of the complaint filed by Manju T S/o Tippeswamy.
Ex.P2 is the OPD card issued by Government Hospital, Nelamangala in which appearance of the petitioner with injuries suffered in a road traffic accident on 19.09.2020 is noted.
Ex.P3 is the Discharge Summary issued by KIMS, Bengaluru in which reason for the injury suffered by the petitioner is noted as alleged RTA on 19.09.2020 at 10.15 PM near Nelamangala are mentioned.

Ex.R1 is the copy of the notice issued under Sec. 133 of IMV Act by SHO., Nelamangala Traffic Police Station to respondent No.1 intimating to produce documents with respect to motorcycle No. KA-52-R-8514 against which Crime No. 334/2020 for the offence punishable u/Secs 279, 337 IPC has been registered.

Ex.R2 is the Reply dated 10.07.2020 issued by respondent No.1 to the notice issued u/S 133 of IMV Act by SHO., Nelamangala Traffic Police Station.
16.

Ex.P148 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Nelamangala Traffic Police in Crime No.334/2020 against Paramesh S/o Gangaiah, rider of the moped No. KA-52-R- 8541 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 IPC and Sec. 181 of IMV Act.

Ex.P149 is the copy of the order sheet pertaining to CC No. 5058/2020 on the file of II. Addl. Civil Judge & JMFC.,
Nelgmangala registered against Paramesh on the basis of the chargesheet filed by Nelamangala Traffic Police in Crime No. 334/2020 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec. 279,
337, 338 IPC and Sec. 181 of IMV Act.
Ex.P150 is the copy of spot mahazar dated 20.09.2020.

Ex.P154 to P156 are the statement of respondent No.1 Manjula W/o Paramesh, Paramesh S/o Gangaiah, Shivaprakash S/o Laxmanappa, Narasegowda S/o Gangaiah, Manu B S/o Buddanna B T,
Manju T S/o Tippeswamy - petitioner.
Ex.P157 is the copy of the Wound Certificate.
17. In this case, at this stage there are no evidence to disbelieve the contents of the police records and evidence of petitioner regarding the reason and mode of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 19.09.2020 at 10 PM when petitioner was riding motorcycle No.KA-05-JK- 6048 on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-4 National Highway near T. Begur in front of TCI godown, Nagamangala Paramesh negligently rode the moped No. KA-52-R-8514, dashed the same to motorcycle No.KA-05-JK-6048 thereby caused accident and caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative and Issue No.2 in the Negative.

18. Issue No.3: In the lengthy arguments learned advocate appearing for the petitioner by analyzing the evidence in the file requested to award compensation as claimed in the application by relying on Manu.B vs Manjula on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98781910/
4 the following judgments: -
a) AIR 2009 SC 2819 - Bimla Devi and others vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others DD 15.04.2009 b) AIR 2011 SC 1504 - Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand and others.

In the lengthy arguments learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 by analyzing the evidence available in the file submitted that the petitioner is not entitle to receive compensation from respondent No.2 by relying on the following judgments: -
a) MFA No. 3297/2014 (MV-D) - Smt. Adilakshmamma and others vs. Raju B and another DD 13.04.2023 b) 2018(1) Kar.LR 249 - The Oriental Insurance Co.

sentences.text: In the light of the judgments cited above with reference to the submission made on behalf of both contesting parties, I have appreciate the evidence available on record.

21. In the evidence affidavit, petitioner/ PW.1 stated that in the accident he has suffered severe diffuse injury, Post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur with left condylar and parasymphysis and right subcondylar fracture, took first aid at Government Hospital, Nelamangala then took treatment at KIM, Bengaluru as an inpatient by spending approximately Rs.1,95,000/- for treatment Rs.35,436/- for conveyance and required to take further treatment, on the date of accident he used to earn Rs.17,000/- per month by working in a private company.
22. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 denied the allegations regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
23. In the cross-examination petitioner/P.W.1 stated about non-production of inpatient bill of KIMS Hospital.
PW.1 denied about the prescriptions regarding the bill produced at Ex.P40.
PW.1 denied the suggestion that bill marked at Ex.P49 is not concerned to him.

Manu.B vs Manjula on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98781910/
5 24.

In the evidence affidavit, PW.2 Dr. Ravish V.N. stated that since 20.09.2020 to 26.09.2020 then from 02.01.2021 to 07.01.2021 at KIMS Hospital he has treated the petitioner for fracture of shaft of left femur with left condyle of mandible with dislocation of TM joint with fracture of right ramus oro maxillary region.
PW.2 stated that on 08.06.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability of 12.13% to whole body.
In the evidence PW.2 produced case sheets, OPD Card, Disability evaluation form, X-rays at Ex.P158 to P161.

In the cross-examination PW.2 stated that petitioner is not required to take further follow-up treatment and stated about non-production of the documents regarding physiotherapy taken by the petitioner.
PW.2 stated that normally 6 to 9 months required to heal the fractures.
PW.2 admitted that as on 08.06.2023 fractures of the petitioner are united and submitted ignorance about the occupation of the petitioner.
25. In the evidence RW.1 Officer of the insurance company stated nothing regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

26. Wound Certificate, OPD book, Discharge Summary, medical certificate, medical bills inpatient files, X-ray and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of shaft of left femur with left condyle of mandible with dislocation of TM joint with fracture of right ramus oro maxillary region, took first aid at Government Hospital, Nelamangala, then took treatment at KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru from 20.09.2020 to 26.09.2020, 02.01.2021 to 07.01.2021 by spending approximately Rs.166,700/-.

In the xerox copy of the Driving License date of birth of petitioner is noted as 29.04.1998.
27.
In the file there are no evidence to show either decrease in the salary or termination from the employment by the employer of the petitioner.
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.2 and medical certificate issued by the PW.2 are insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

Hence, I award Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,66,700/-
towards treatment, Rs.30,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment, Rs.97,000/-
(Rs.14,500/- x 6) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.80,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.4,73,700/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as compensation.

28. Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R4 shows that as on the date of accident moped No.
KA-52-R-8514 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.

The police have filed chargesheet marked at Ex.P148 alleging that Paramesh S/o Gangaiah rode TVS moped No.KA-52-R- 8514 without having license drove the same and thereby committed offence punishable u/S. 181 of IMV Act and Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC.

In the reply submitted to the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act dated 10.07.2020 marked at Ex.R2 the respondent No.1 Smt.Manjula noted non-possessing of license by Paramesh S/o Gangaiah to ride the moped No. KA-52-R-8514.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on 19.09.2020 the date of accident Paramesh had license to drive the moped No.KA- 52-R-8514.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident respondent No.1 Manjula has violated the driver clause of the policy.

Therefore, the judgments cited by respondent No.2 are Manu.B vs Manjula on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98781910/
6 applicable to the facts of the present case.

sentences.text: Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 owner of the moped No.KA-52-R-8514 who violated the terms of the policy regarding the driver clause is not entitle to be indemnified from the respondent No.2 insurance company, therefore, the respondent No.1 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed in the following terms.

The respondent No.1 owner of the moped No. KA-52-R- 8514 shall pay Rs.4,73,700/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Seven Hundred only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner as compensation.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Petition with respect to respondent No.2 the insurance company is hereby dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

Bangalore.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed in the following terms.

The respondent No.1 owner of the moped No. KA-52-R- 8514 shall pay Rs.4,73,700/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand Seven Hundred only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioner as compensation.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Petition with respect to respondent No.2 the insurance company is hereby dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
